A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPTKB research. All supplied main-text and appendix pages are readable, and the methods, tables, figures and relocated analyses can be reliably matched despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V3 reports original GPTKB construction statistics, entity/triple verification, taxonomy evaluation and content analyses. Appendix E also reports experiments comparing three LLMs.

after.justification: V4 retains original construction and evaluation results and adds a repeated-elicitation consistency experiment in Section 6.1.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds upper and lower clipping to the adaptive similarity threshold used for relation and class clustering. This changes a consolidation component; recursive elicitation, NER, taxonomy construction and entity deduplication retain their procedures.

E1.justification: The open-domain named-entity coverage, Wikidata/web verification and cross-model comparison tasks remain the same. The new consistency check repeats elicitation for the existing Vannevar Bush entity, and the added property breakdowns analyze retained KB content.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same KB comparators. Table 4 retains GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.1 70B and GPT-4o with identical comparison entries, moving from Appendix E to Section 6.3. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported clustering configuration changes from alpha = 1.2 to 1.4 and introduces bounds of 0.75 and 0.95. A new consistency evaluation fixes one subject and measures output volume and exact-match overlap. Existing verification and cross-model comparison settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that those evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 6.1 adds a focused case study of repeated elicitation, testing stability of triple counts and content and reporting parsing failures. Section 5.2 also expands property-distribution analysis, including film-specific properties. The BFS class-distribution analysis already existed in v3's Appendix B.

E5.justification: V4 newly reports 100 elicitation attempts and cluster means with standard deviations: 21 triples with standard deviation 1, and 38 with standard deviation 6. This adds variability reporting absent from v3. However, the listed 52 runs, 32 runs and 10 parsing failures total only 94, leaving the run accounting unclear.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially revises the reported consolidation outcome: relations increase from 1,804 to 567K and classes from 473 to 4,715. Mean label length changes from 24.5 to 21.8, and class/property counts and rankings change throughout Section 5.2. Figure 6 adds property counts, while Section 6.1 adds consistency findings, including 0.67 exact-match overlap. Main precision rates and Table 4 remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish a comparable-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises the mathematical definition of its threshold by clipping the frequency-scaled expression between lower and upper bounds. This is a limited formal revision. The storage-capacity calculation and its theoretical caveat remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V4 narrows the advertised contribution toward LLM knowledge analysis, removing the abstract/conclusion claims of advancing general-domain KB construction and explicitly listing consistency among the analyses. The central materialization claim and the 101M-triple, 2.9M-entity resource remain; the cost-efficiency claim is retained in Section 6.2.

C2.justification: Section 8 removes substantial qualifications about probabilistic-to-binary materialization, few-shot prompt bias, missing document provenance, uncertain absolute precision and downstream unsuitability. Precision and consistency problems remain discussed elsewhere. V4 adds interpretations concerning prompt-dependent lower bounds, archival value and exact-match consistency underestimating semantic agreement, substantially changing the stated limitations and applicability framing.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 adds explicit clipping limits and updates the clustering hyperparameter, improving specification of that component. The appendix prompts, batch configuration, reported 27-hour/$3,500 execution, TTL download, access interfaces and resource license are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds works by Singhania, Hao, Carta, Zhang and Funk, extending discussion of LM-KBC, LLM-based extraction and ontology construction. It also contrasts generating a taxonomy with incorporating existing classes and removes the specific criticism of Wu's prompting approach from the limitations. Wu's 2024-to-2025 reference update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: V4 substantially recasts the narrative through a new title, revised abstract and conclusion, and a rewritten limitations section with named paragraphs. It renames Sections 3 and 6.2, expands graph-exploration explanations, and integrates the former appendix discussions of BFS class distributions and other LLMs into the main text.

P2.justification: V4 adds the three-panel property-distribution Figure 6 and revises the categories and proportions in Figure 4. The BFS chart moves from v3 Figure 7 to v4 Figure 5, and Table 4 moves into the main text. Other diagrams, appendix screenshots and prompt displays are retained, within the same overall two-column design.

improvement.justification: V4 provides more explicit clustering controls, richer content summaries and a useful new consistency check. However, that check's listed groups account for only 94 of the stated 100 runs, and Section 8 removes important provenance, precision and downstream-use qualifications. The substantially revised consolidation statistics are not accompanied by evidence establishing better quality. These benefits and losses leave the overall quality direction unclear.
